note: Canonical coordinate contract for the IRX visual asset system. compose_frame.py reads ONLY this file to place assets. If a frame needs an offset that is not in here, the contract is wrong — fix the contract, not the frame.

canvas.rationale: Phase 1 defines no canvas. 16:9 chosen for the investor demo surface (ScenarioDemo + deck). Mobile crops to a 4:5 safe area, documented below.

safeArea.note: Anything narratively load-bearing must sit inside mobile_4_5. Slot 'centre' is centred within it.

layerNote: Phase 1 established no layer convention, so the Phase 2A brief's list is adopted with changes forced by the artwork: (1) character_face/character_hair are NOT separate top-level layers - a register is one atomic swappable unit and splitting it would let face and hair desynchronise; (2) 'furniture' sits AFTER character_head so the counter occludes the figure below counter height; (3) 'character_front' (hands) sits after 'prop' so hands rest on the counter surface; (4) ADDED IN QA: 'character_contact' between prop and character_front carries contact shadows. Without it the figure read as pasted onto the background. 'character_back' carries the figure's cast shadow on the wall.

basePoint.note: bottom-centre; lands on the scene slot anchor

register.note: A register may apply its own rotation about neckAnchor (declared as data-register-rotate on the root <g>). Rotation about the anchor keeps the join mechanical while allowing head tilt to carry part of the register.

occlusionLine.note: counter top surface. Figures at left/centre/right are occluded below this by the 'furniture' layer.

scene.kitchen.propNote: The environment owns prop placement, exactly as it owns character slots. Props declare a bottom-centre anchor and are placed onto a named scene anchor.
